title.narrative: Second Bangladesh Green and Climate Resilient Development Credit

description.narrative: The development objective of the Second Bangladesh Green and Climate Resilient Development Credit Project is to support the government of Bangladesh in transitioning to green and climate-resilient development. This will be achieved by enhancing public planning, financing, and delivery of green and climate-resilient interventions, and promoting key sector reforms for clean and resource-efficient production and services. The project aligns with Bangladesh's 8th Five-Year Plan (FY21–25), which aims to eliminate extreme poverty, achieve upper-middle-income country status by 2031, and high-income country status by 2041. The plan includes comprehensive structural reforms to accelerate sustainable growth, build climate resilience, enhance public services, and manage the environment and natural resources better. The Development Policy Credit (DPC) series supports priority areas of the Government Program, contributing to the 8th FYP, Bangladesh Delta Plan 2100 (BDP), National Adaptation Plan (NAP), and Nationally Determined Contribution (NDCs) by integrating green and climate resilience priorities in public investment planning, incentivizing local actions, enabling access to carbon markets, promoting sustainable public procurement, and setting a legal and institutional framework for effective implementation. The project is aligned with the WBG Country Partnership Framework (CPF) FY23–FY27 and the goals of the Paris Agreement, incorporating lessons from previous DPCs in Bangladesh and other countries.

To support the Government of Bangladesh to transition to green and climate resilient development by (a) enhancing public planning, financing, and delivery of green and climate resilient interventions; and (b) promoting key sector reforms for clean and resource efficient production and services.

title.narrative: Urban Local Government Institutions (City Corporations and Category A Pourashavas) spending more than 10 percent of block-grant resources on GCR projects

comment.narrative: The Ministry of Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives (MoLGRDC) issued the “Guidelines for Green and Climate Resilient Project Planning, Formulation, Financing, and Implementation for Urban Local Government Institutions (City Corporations and Paurashavas), 2024” on June 3, 2024. The guideline is now being implemented to strengthen climate resilience in urban local governments, contributing to Bangladesh's broader sustainability and GCR goals by encouraging urban local governments to expand resources for GCR projects and prioritize climate financing. Furthermore, a guideline on “Performance Criteria in the Formulae to Incentivize GCR Priority Expenditures at Local Governments” was delivered in June 2024. The guidelines are binding for all City Corporations and Pourashavas. However, no concrete data is available at this stage to assess the status of the percentage of block-grant resources spent by urban local government institutions.

title.narrative: New municipalities with at least 80 percent cost recovery on operations and maintenance

comment.narrative: The Municipal Water Supply Management Guideline and Municipal Fecal Sludge and Sanitation Management Guideline were approved and issued by the Local Govt. Division (LGD) of Ministry of LGRD&C on March 14, 2023 through an Office Circular. These guidelines are applicable for all 330 municipalities of Bangladesh. In line with these guidelines, draft Water Supply and Sanitation management (WSS) by-laws have been prepared by Dept. of Public Health Engineering (DPHE) and circulated to 30 municipalities. 30 municipalities have developed their tariff adjustment framework. Out of 30, 15 municipalities have had their tariff framework endorsed by respective District Commissioner's (DC) offices. Therefore, 15 municipalities have finalized their respective WSS by-laws including Tariff Frameworks and have submitted the by-laws to the line ministry. Chowgachha, Gangni and Nachole municipalities have at least 80 percent recovery on operations and maintenance.

title.narrative: Women-owned businesses submitting bids in public procurement per fiscal year

comment.narrative: Data is not yet available at this stage, and full results will depend on the associated policy trigger of DPC3. However, the BPPA will procure an NGO to support women-owned businesses through activities under the World Bank-financed Strengthening Institutions for Transparency and Accountability (SITA) project. The TOR will be developed for firms to provide advocacy, technical support and procurement support to women-owned business on how to register in e-GP and prepare bids. The KPI in BPPA's contractual agreement with the selected NGO will measure how many women-owned business have registered and submitted bids in the public procurement.

title.narrative: Procurement processes of selected Public-Sector Organizations using SPP rated criteria in relevant contracts per fiscal year

comment.narrative: The Bank is working with the key sectors to prepare sector-specific strategies to implement SPP. A Training of Trainers was delivered to staff in the key ministries on SPP and focus groups were formed under the CSF grant. The building sector-specific SPP strategy/guidance note is being finalized and will be used for the upcoming building /infrastructure procurement under World Bank-financed projects and Public Procurement in FY26/27. The guidance notes for other sectors, such as energy, transport etc. will be developed by the Ministry of Planning by March 2026.

title.narrative: Industry units, project facilities and individuals inspected by DoE's Enforcement Wing and mobile courts for environmental compliance per calendar year

comment.narrative: To support implementation of the Enforcement Guidelines issued by MOEFCC in November 2024, DOE's Monitoring and Enforcement Wing (MEW) conducted two training events for 200 magistrates, prosecutors, and field officers on EG-related procedures. DOE commenced online hearings from August 4, 2025 on a trial basis. MEW will align monthly enforcement bulletins with EG-recommended disclosure formats, add quarterly disclosures, and compile annual reports. For FY25-26, MEW set district-level, quarterly disaggregated enforcement targets based on self-determined inputs. From FY26-27 onward, Annual Enforcement Plans (AEPs) will fully follow EG guidance. The number of DOE's environmental compliance inspections in calendar year 2024 reduced to 4,550, which may be attributed to the temporary halt of all administrative activities across the government following political unrest in July 2024. However, the inspection cases are expected to increase in calendar year 2025.

title.narrative: BDP projects with Development Project Proformas approved by ECNEC, based on 5-year re-prioritized investment program and ADM principles

comment.narrative: The Planning Division of the Ministry of Planning (MoP) has approved the Project/Program Selection Committee (PPSC) and adopted a Delta Appraisal Framework (DAF), and the govt. circular was issued on November 7, 2024. The PPSC will determine if a project is aligned with BDP2100 by using the DAF tools. However, no project has been processed using DAF as of date. One of the key reasons for the delayed execution of DAF is the absence of an associated operational manual for the use of the DAF. Therefore, the General Economic Division (GED) of the Ministry of Planning has deployed a consulting firm, i.e., Institute of Water Modelling (IWM), to prepare a DAF manual and conduct Training of Trainers (ToT) for concerned officials of various ministries and selected agencies. After the completion of the DAF manual and necessary training, the DAF will be used to appraise Delta projects.

title.narrative: Carbon emission reduction credits registered, approved, authorized, and transferred through the domestic system

comment.narrative: The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) continues to advance the Article 6 agenda through the approval of key documents (including A6 Roadmap, standardized templates for A6 transaction, methodologies, etc.). A solar home system (SHS) project has been registered under the domestic system, Bangladesh-owned Standardized Crediting Framework (SCF), which is one of the key steps in completing an A6-aligned carbon transaction. The project is now undergoing verification by a third-party verifier, using the approved SHS methodology. Once verification is completed, the project will be submitted for the approval and authorization by MoEFCC, before the transfer of carbon credit transaction in FY26.
